title: Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Amendment (Australian Grape and Wine Authority) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update excise levy legislation to support the proposed Australian Grape and Wine Authority, allowing collected levies to be paid to that authority.
It would replace references and definitions linked to the Wine Australia Corporation and remove its special process for recommending levy rates after annual general meetings.
The levy amendments would take effect with the main merger bill’s provisions on 1 July 2014, without altering the structure or amounts of existing levies.
changes: The representative organisation definition for the grapes research levy would be aligned with the new authority’s legislation.
The old Corporation definition would be removed from the wine grapes levy schedule.
The declared winemakers’ organisation definition would refer to the new authority’s governing Act.
summary.affected: Grape growers and winemakers paying the relevant levies, their representative organisations and the Australian Grape and Wine Authority are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Introduced a companion bill updating the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act 1999 to replace references to the Wine Australia Corporation with the new Australian Grape and Wine Authority, and removed the requirement for Wine Australia's annual meeting to recommend levy rate changes.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Supported bills merging the Grape and Wine Research and Development Corporation and Wine Australia into a new Australian Grape and Wine Authority from 1 July 2014, following an August 2012 industry submission from the Winemakers' Federation and Wine Grape Growers Australia, while noting the coalition had little time to scrutinise the legislation.

speeches.speaker: Nick Champion
speeches.brief: Supported the bills merging the Grape and Wine Research and Development Corporation and Wine Australia into the Australian Grape and Wine Authority from 1 July 2014, and said the wine industry, centred in the Barossa and Clare valleys, faced a persistently high Australian dollar with some 19 central banks now holding it as a reserve currency.

speeches.speaker: Bob Baldwin
speeches.brief: Supported the wine authority merger bills, noting Australia is the world's No. 4 wine-exporting country and, for Chinese tourists, the world's No. 2 food and wine tourism destination after France, and cited a World Economic Forum report showing Australia's innovation capacity ranking had fallen from 27th to 32nd globally.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: Supported the wine authority merger bills, which will have a combined budget of close to $35 million, and warned that the carbon tax could add close to $500,000 to the electricity bill of a large winery, while a supermarket duopoly controlling 60 to 70 per cent of wine sales was harming smaller producers.
